_comment: 英文覆盖层：按索引对齐 foods/scenes/unis 的中文条目（本文件数组顺序必须与 zh 文件一致）。覆盖 desc/history 叙述字段；名称用各条目已有的 en 字段。
foods: Red oil bubbling, numbing and spicy — a whole table around one pot. Chengdu's liveliest way to eat.
Numbing, spicy, hot and tender. 'Chen Mapo' created this world-famous dish 150 years ago.
Noodles once carried on a shoulder pole through the streets, with pickled veggies, minced pork and chili oil.
Skewers of all kinds swished in a red-oil pot — you pay by counting the sticks. Chengdu at its most down-to-earth.
Thin-skinned Sichuan wontons, silky and tender, in clear broth or red oil. The old flagship shop is on Chunxi Road.
Pork dumplings in sweet red-oil soy sauce — a century-old taste, salty, sweet and slightly spicy.
Sliced beef and offal in chili oil with crushed peanuts. Named after a couple who sold it from a street stall.
Little round cakes baked in a copper street pan, crispy outside, soft inside. Students' favorite snack.
Sticky-rice balls thrown at the counter with three loud 'bangs' — the farther they fly, the better the maker.
Braised rabbit head, spicy or five-spice. 'Nibbling rabbit heads' is a true Chengdu pleasure.
scenes: A 2,200-year-old irrigation system built by Li Bing, which turned the plain into the 'Land of Abundance'. A World Heritage Site.
Home of the giant pandas — watch cubs climb and tumble. Panda fans from all over the world come here.
The only shrine in China where a ruler and his minister are worshipped together: Liu Bei and Zhuge Liang. A Three-Kingdoms pilgrimage site.
A Qing-dynasty style street beside Wuhou Shrine — lanterns, snacks and a beautiful night view.
The cottage where the poet Du Fu lived in Chengdu. He wrote his famous 'Broad mansions for all' poem here.
Wide Alley, Narrow Alley and Well Alley from the Qing 'Manchu City' — a living fossil of old Chengdu life.
One of the birthplaces of Taoism. 'Qingcheng, the most serene mountain under heaven' — temples hidden in deep woods.
Ruins of the ancient Shu kingdom. The Golden Sun Bird was unearthed here — now the symbol of Chengdu.
Heming Teahouse has served tea for a century. Ear-cleaning, chatting — the most 'Chengdu' afternoon ever.
A Ming-dynasty covered bridge over the Jin River, full of restaurants and bars, glowing like a treasure ship at night.
